item.content:encoded: The comedy was excellent, but I have one tiny problem with this. In Experiment 702-040, it states that SCP-702 gave back the exact same nails as in Experiment 702-037. However, the 037 experiment included books, not nails. The first nail experiment occurred in 038, not 037. I just wanted to point this out.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Came to say this ^ exactly.

Only interpretation that makes a bit of sense is that 702-1 is kidding and Dr. Sanders is falling for it. But that would mean gullibility nearing incompetence.

A better end note would be "Examination of pre-experiment documentation confirms model was non-anomalous." That way the highly-educated researcher doesn't have to take a turn with the idiot ball, and we get interesting implications that trade items act differently once they get wherever -1 takes them.

item.content:encoded: Last entry (working miniature 914) doesn't make much sense to me. "No anomalous properties" would imply "doesn't do anything interesting when we work it like the real one". While I can roll with some silliness, that's just not in character for researchers that poke and prod everything that comes out of 914…

item.content:encoded:
From the description:
Some objects are rejected by SCP-702-1, claiming that it "already has one", and demands a new gift, returning the offered object.

So offering something it already has is not going to get you "off". The Trader does not go back until you give it something it wants, or it DATA EXPUNGES you.
